title: Ruy Lopez: Exchange Variation
line: White gives the bishop for the knight to spoil Black's pawns, and aims for an endgame.

steps.text: The Ruy Lopez: Black asks the bishop what it will do.
Take the knight. You give up the bishop to spoil Black's pawns.

also.b5a4: Keeping the bishop is the main line, in other lessons. This lesson takes the knight.

steps.text: Tap the two black pawns that stand on the same file, one in front of the other.
steps.after: Doubled pawns. After the center pawns trade, your four pawns to three on the king side can make a free pawn; Black's doubled ones cannot.

steps.text: The pawn on e5 looks free, but it is not. If your knight takes it, the queen attacks the knight and the pawn on e4, and gets a pawn back.
So castle instead, and leave the pawn for now.

also.b1c3: That is also played. This lesson castles first.
also.d2d3: That is also played. This lesson castles first.

steps.after: Castled, you threaten the pawn: if the queen then grabs yours on e4, the rook comes to e1 and drives her off. Black guards with a pawn.

steps.text: Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares to open the center.
Take back with the knight, which stands well in the center.
Step the knight back, out of the way of the queens.

also.d4e2: That square is also played. This lesson goes to b3.

steps.text: Take back the queen with your rook, which lands on the open file.
steps.after: Queens are off. In the end your extra pawn on the king side can become a pawn no black pawn can stop.

summary: The bishop is given for the knight to double Black's pawns. With queens traded, White's pawns count for more.
